newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Harvest picks up. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Harvest picks up. [CORRECTED 14:15 GMT]

text.p: Harvest of hard red winter wheat was picking up speed Wednesday as warm, dry weather prevailed over the central U.S. Plains, grain merchandisers said.
"We're rocking and rolling. We've got a south wind, temperatures in the 90s (Farenheit). That should allow us to keep cutting statewide," an Oklahoma dealer said.

Temperatures of 90 degrees F or higher and winds of five to 15 miles per hour were on tap Wednesday and Thursday for Kansas, and dealers said those weather conditions should help dry down the crop and prepare it for harvest.
"I expect we'll be test cutting over a wide area (of Kansas) this weekend," a south central Kansas dealer said.
Meanwhile, basis bids for HRW wheat were steady to weaker Wednesday. (Corrects day from Thursday)
